# Which gametype settings the menu can reach — and which it cannot

**Generated by `tools/settings-xref.py`, against `ate47/bocw-source`, 2026-09-08.** Re-run it rather
than trusting this table if the dump moves.

klaze measured from inside the game that a **Gunfight** lobby shows a round-timer row, a **3v3
Gunfight** lobby does not, and **no** lobby shows a per-side team cap. Those are statements about the
*menu*. This note separates the menu from the settings, mechanically, for all 463 of them at once.

---

## The mapping is exact — that is what makes this trustworthy

A bundle's `setting` field **is** the `getgametypesetting()` key. Proven by a plain-named pair:

| | |
|---|---|
| `scriptbundle/gamesettings/allow_ingame_team_change.json` | `"setting": "allowInGameTeamChange"` |
| `scripts/mp_common/gametypes/serversettings.gsc:43` | `getgametypesetting( #"allowingameteamchange" )` |

Script hashes lowercase before hashing (ACTS `hash_mini.hpp`), so the camelCase bundle name and the
lowercase script name are the same key. No inference involved.

## The counts

```
463  distinct settings read or written by script
427  menu bundles  (395 carry a distinct `setting`)

130  plain-named, HAS a menu row      -> the lobby can set it, IF the playlist shows that row
 97  plain-named, NO menu row         -> a real setting with no lobby path
236  still hashed, NO menu row        -> and 0 of 236 matched any bundle
```

## 🔓 The rule that falls out: **hashed ⇒ hidden**

**Not one** of the 236 hashed keys is explained by a menu row. That is not luck. A setting with a menu
row has its name spelled out in the bundle — which is exactly where the dump's resolver finds names.
So a key that is *still* a hash in the dump is a key with no bundle, i.e. **no menu row**.

⚠ This gives the project a cheap classifier it did not have: **you can tell whether a setting is
menu-reachable by whether the dump resolved its name.** No lobby walk required.

✅ **It independently confirms klaze's observation.** `#"hash_3a4691a853585241"`
(**`maxsquadplayers`**) is hashed → hidden → no lobby exposes it. klaze walked the lobby and found no
per-side cap row. Two methods, opposite directions, same answer.

⚠ **"No menu row" is NOT "unreachable".** `setgametypesetting()` takes any key at runtime, and
`#"timelimit"` is the standing proof. It means the *lobby* cannot set it. Nothing more.

## 🔓 New this pass — cracked, and directly usable

### `#"hash_3b05ecbff72f1065"` = **`gunfightloadoutindex`**
Exact 63-bit FNV1a64 match (`tools/crack-hash.py`). `gunfight.gsc:83`:

```gsc
bundle_index = isdefined( getgametypesetting( #"hash_3b05ecbff72f1065" ) ) ? getgametypesetting( #"hash_3b05ecbff72f1065" ) : 0;
var_92d79c8a = getscriptbundle( "gunfightloadoutlist" );
bundle_name = isdefined( var_92d79c8a.var_d6f55369[ bundle_index ].loadout ) ? ... : "mp_gunfight_loadout_default";
```

`scriptbundle/gunfightloadoutlist/gunfightloadoutlist.json` holds **four** entries:

| index | bundle | in plain terms |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `mp_gunfight_loadout_default` | the stock rotation |
| 1 | `mp_gunfight_loadout_snipers` | **snipers only** |
| 2 | `mp_gunfight_loadouts_blueprints` | blueprint weapons |
| 3 | `mp_gunfight_loadout_melee` | **melee only** |

**`uint:5` in `mp_custom_game.ddl:3554`** (holds 0–31; only 0–3 are backed by an entry — a higher
index falls through the `isdefined` to the default bundle rather than erroring).

🔓 **This is a new mod feature for one `setgametypesetting` call**, and there is no other way to reach
it — no menu row exists.

⚠ **Timing matters.** `gunfight.gsc:81` wraps the whole block in `if ( !isdefined( game.var_96a8ff4a ) )`,
and `game.` scope survives across rounds. Our hook runs at `globallogic.gsc:5536`, **before**
`onstartgametype` at `:5537`, so the first match of a lobby is reachable. For a later match in the
same lobby the latch is already set — clear `game.var_96a8ff4a` in the hook as well as writing the
setting. **Untested either way.**

### `gunfight_spy_plane` publishes 3 of the 4 values it declares
`optionscount: 3`, but `value4: "3"` exists with `label4: menu/shared`:

| value | label | in menu? |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Disabled | yes |
| 1 | Enabled | yes |
| 2 | *(hash label)* | yes |
| **3** | **Shared** | **NO** |

`gunfight.gsc:48` reads it into `level.gunfightspyplane`. So `setgametypesetting( #"gunfightspyplane", 3 )`
reaches a spy-plane mode the menu will not offer. Same shape as `time_limit_seconds` publishing 6 of 20.

### Two hashes that did NOT crack
Reported as misses, per the tool's own doctrine — **a miss means the wordlist was wrong.**

| hash | what it does | candidates tried |
|---|---|---|
| `hash_7647d0e9a45eeca6` | `challenges.gsc:108` → `level.var_9ff21849`. When set, scoring goes placement-based (`challenges.gsc:4598` top-3) and the game behaves like DM. Smells like a Fireteam/squad-placement flag. | 14,969 + 10,682 harvested |
| `hash_6e051e440a6c3b91` | `player_shared.gsc:43` → `level.var_7d3ed2bf`, gated on `currentsessionmode() != 4`. See the Route A caveat below. | 14,971 + 10,682 harvested |

## ⚠ Corrections to what this project had recorded

### The join gate is `team_assignment.gsc:95–126`, not `:148`
`:148` is `return #"spectator";` — the *fallback* at the end of `function_ccb3bc7a`, not a gate.
`.claude/CLAUDE.md`'s own citation (`team_assignment.gsc:94`) was right; the `:148` in
[`lobby-settings.md`](lobby-settings.md) and [`test-queue.md`](test-queue.md) was mine and is fixed.

### The gate has TWO checks, and only one was recorded
```gsc
function function_efe5a681( team )                       // team_assignment.gsc:95
{
    max_players = player::function_d36b6597();           // -> com_maxclients (8)
    team_players = getplayers( team );
    if ( team_players.size >= max_players && max_players != 0 ) return false;   // :100  RECORDED
    if ( !max_players ) return true;
    available_spots = function_ee150fcc( team_players );  // :110  NOT recorded
    party = self getparty();
    if ( party.var_a15e4438 > available_spots ) return false;                   // :113  NOT recorded
    return true;
}
```

✅ **Route A survives.** `function_ee150fcc` (`:76`) is `com_maxclients − function_1cec6cba(team_players)`
— **also 8**, not `maxsquadplayers`. For a solo player (`party.var_a15e4438 == 1`) the second check
fails only when the team already holds 8, identical to the first. **Both gates are 8.**

⚠ `function_46edfa55` (`:86`) is the `maxsquadplayers` version of the same helper — and it is used
**only** in the squad-distribution path (`:747`), never in the join gate. The project's probe comment
citing `team_assignment.gsc:864` for this is off; the real lines are `:731`, `:745–747`, `:777`, `:889–902`.

### ⚠ NEW RISK to Route A — a party can occupy a whole side
`player_shared.gsc:1335`:
```gsc
function private function_c70c4c93( party )
{
    max_players = function_d36b6597();
    if ( isdefined( level.var_7d3ed2bf ) && level.var_7d3ed2bf && !party.fill ) return max_players;  // 8!
    return party.var_a15e4438;
}
```
`function_1cec6cba` sums this **per distinct party**. So if `level.var_7d3ed2bf` is on and a party has
`fill == 0`, that one party counts as **8** toward the team and `available_spots` goes to **0** —
nobody else joins that side, regardless of how few people are actually on it.

`level.var_7d3ed2bf` = `getgametypesetting( #"hash_6e051e440a6c3b91" )`, gated on
`currentsessionmode() != 4`. **Whether it is on in a private custom game is unknown** — probe it
(lobby_probe bit 1 of probe 0). If Route A fails with players who queued as a party but works for
solo joiners, **this is the first thing to check.**

## 🔓 `maxplayers` — one call site, plain name, and two different widths

`challenges.gsc:109` is the **only** `getgametypesetting( #"maxplayers" )` in the dump.

```gsc
level.var_9ff21849 = ... getgametypesetting( #"hash_7647d0e9a45eeca6" ) ...    // :108
level.max_players  = getgametypesetting( #"maxplayers" );                       // :109
if ( level.var_9ff21849 && ... && level.var_704bcca1 > 0 )
    level.var_77e0887f = level.max_players / level.var_704bcca1;                // :113
```

🔓 **`maxplayers ÷ maxsquadplayers` is the engine's own expression for "number of teams."** That is
structural corroboration, from a file with nothing to do with team assignment, that
**`maxsquadplayers` is per-team size.**

✅ **And it fits every cap klaze measured**, with `maxplayers = 2 × cap`:

| lobby | observed per-side cap | ⇒ predicted `maxsquadplayers` | ⇒ predicted `maxplayers` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gunfight | 2 | **2** | 4 |
| Gunfight 3v3 | 3 | **3** | 6 |
| CDL Pro S&D | 4 | **4** | 8 |
| TDM | unrestricted | **6** | 12 |

⚠ **A model that fits four points is a hypothesis, not a measurement.** `lobby_probe` probes 6 and 7
read both numbers directly. **Run it in two different lobbies** — one reading cannot tell the cap from
a coincidence.

### The DDL widths disagree between structs, and it matters
| field | `custom_games.ddl` | `mp_custom_game.ddl` | `mp_gametype_settings.ddl` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `maxplayers` | **`uint:4`** (max 15) | **`uint:7`** (max 127) | present |
| `maxsquadplayers` (`hash_3a46…`) | `uint:6` (max 63) | `uint:6` | present |
| `maxteamplayers` | **absent** | `uint:6` | present |
| `gunfightloadoutindex` (`hash_3b05…`) | **absent** | `uint:5` | present |

✅ The project's original asymmetry claim is **correct**: `maxsquadplayers` is in `custom_games.ddl`
and `maxteamplayers` is not.

⚠ **`max_players.json` publishes 1–12 while the MP struct stores `uint:7` (127).** Same
menu-filters-storage shape as `timelimit`. But `custom_games.ddl` stores only `uint:4` (15), so
**which struct a custom lobby actually serializes decides the real ceiling** — and that is not
readable from the dump. L2 measures it.

## Settings with no menu row that are worth a probe

Everything here is **plain-named** (bucket B), so `setgametypesetting()` takes it verbatim.

| setting | read at | why it is interesting |
|---|---|---|
| `teamcount` | `globallogic.gsc:233` | sets `level.multiteam` (`> 2`). The one setting that could make Gunfight multiteam — which is the *only* condition under which `level.maxteamplayers` is enforced |
| `maxteamplayers` | `globallogic.gsc:240` | inert for a 2-team mode, live the moment `teamcount > 2` |
| `maxplayers` | `challenges.gsc:109` | above |
| `playerkillsmax` / `totalkillsmax` | `sd.gsc:641–642` | S&D-only; shows how deep the per-gametype hidden settings go |
| `maxuniquerolesperteam` | `player_role.gsc:102` | a per-team number nothing in this project has looked at |

⚠ Reading `teamcount` and `maxteamplayers` is free (probe them). **Writing `teamcount` is not** — it
runs at `globallogic.gsc:233`, before our hook, and changing what `level.multiteam` means mid-match
touches spawn, scoring and HUD paths. If it is ever tried, it is a **one-write, own-match, lobby-return-tested**
test like everything else in band C.
